span.label: The racial in-group bias in empathic neural response to others' pain, and whether shifting a person's self-construal changes it.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Cultures differ in how strongly people favour their own group's suffering - is the self-construal that distinguishes those cultures the thing actually doing the work?
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Shows the neural in-group bias is not fixed: priming an independent self-construal reduces it in insula, mid-cingulate and SMA, which makes self-construal a candidate cause rather than a correlate.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: self-construal sets where the psychological boundary falls: interdependence draws the line between in-group and out-group, independence draws it between self and all others and so weakens the in-group/out-group split that produces biased empathy
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: independent priming shifts cultural identity toward Western cultures, so Caucasian models are recategorised as in-group and their suffering draws a stronger neural response
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: independent priming weakens race-based group affiliation between the Chinese participants and the Chinese models, dissolving the basis of the in-group advantage
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: empathic concern generates altruistic motivation, so a bias in empathy toward in-group members produces parochial altruism in behaviour
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: an interdependent self organises behaviour by reference to others in one's relationships, which sharpens the in-group/out-group line
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: an independent self organises behaviour by reference to one's own thoughts, which weakens the group boundary and lets a person cross it easily
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the route from bias to behaviour runs through empathy: empathic concern produces altruistic motivation, so a biased empathy yields a parochial altruism
span.note: duplicate of: mechanisms[3]
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: self-construal is treated as temporarily shiftable, not as a fixed cultural trait - a 108-second reading task moves it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The two competing explanations offered for why independent priming shifted responses toward out-group faces are not yet tested
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The reduction of racial bias under independent priming does not license the conclusion that Westerners lack racial in-group bias
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The self-report measures showed no racial in-group bias at all, so the effect rests on the imaging measures
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: One cultural sample: 30 Chinese university students, in a design whose logic is about differences between cultures.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The mechanism linking culture to bias was unknown going in, and the study offers a candidate rather than settling it.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Race is operationalised as Asian versus Caucasian faces in short video clips, which is a narrow stand-in for a social category.

span.label: After interdependent self-construal priming, watching a racial in-group member in pain produced stronger activity than an out-group member in the mid-cingulate cortex, left supplementary motor area and left insula.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Priming independent self-construals abolished that racial in-group bias in neural responses to others' pain.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Priming independent rather than interdependent self-construals both lowered the response to in-group members' pain and raised the response to out-group members' pain, although only the increased mid-cingulate response to out-group faces reached significance across priming conditions.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Subjective ratings of others' pain and of the observer's own unpleasantness showed no racial in-group bias, unlike the brain measures.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Participants' habitual (chronic) self-construal scores were unrelated to how much racial in-group bias their brain activity showed.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Across all conditions, seeing painful compared with non-painful stimulation applied to another person activated the mid-cingulate cortex, bilateral supplementary motor area, bilateral insula/inferior frontal gyrus, bilateral secondary somatosensory cortex, bilateral superior parietal and middle temporal gyri, and bilateral posterior cerebellum.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A whole-brain priming-by-race interaction, at a relaxed voxel threshold, located the same modulation in the left supplementary motor area, left inferior frontal gyrus and right temporo-parietal junction.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: After interdependent priming, in-group pain produced stronger activity than out-group pain in mid-cingulate, left insula and SMA - the bias is present.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: After independent priming the same bias was significantly reduced in the same regions - so it is manipulable within a person, not a stable trait.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The neural bias has behavioural consequences: it predicts willingness to sacrifice for in-group members.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The cultural pattern the study explains: both the empathy bias and parochial altruism are stronger in collectivistic than individualistic settings.
